title: Taylor Swift’s ‘Patient Zero’ Debuts at No. 1 on Billboard Hot 100
summary: Swift scores her 16th leader, dethroning Ella Langley’s record 24-week chart-topper, “Choosin’ Texas.”
body: Taylor Swift ’s “Patient Zero” bounds in at No. 1 on the Billboard Hot 100 , becoming her 16th career leader. The song stops the record reign of Ella Langley’s “Choosin’ Texas,” which has run up an unprecedented 24 weeks atop the Hot 100 since February. “Patient Zero” is one of four new songs on the deluxe version, released Sept. 25, of Swift’s 2025 album, The Life of a Showgirl , dubbed The Life of a Showgirl: The Encore . The set (all versions combined) surges back to No. 1 for a 13th week atop the Billboard 200 chart while its three other new tracks launch in the Hot 100’s top five: “Cleveland!,” “Babylon” and “Pink Clouding,” at Nos. 3, 4 and 5, respectively. Related Taylor Swift’s ‘The Life of a Showgirl’ Returns to No. 1 After ‘Encore’ Reissue Swift boasts the third-most No. 1s in the Hot 100’s history, trailing only The Beatles’ 20 and Mariah Carey’s 19. “Patient Zero” is also Swift’s 10th career No. 1 Hot 100 debut — tying her with Drake for the most. Now up to 74 career Hot 100 top 10s, Swift continues to have the most among women. She has the second-most overall, after Drake’s 90. title: Without Kendrick Lamar — or Drake — How Will Hip-Hop Show Up In the Grammys’ Biggest Categories?
summary: Without an obvious star in contention — and given some of hip-hop’s declines in the past year — the genre’s marquee category chances may be slimmer.
body: “At the end of the day, nothing more powerful than rap music,” Kendrick Lamar said onstage at the 2025 Grammys. “We are the culture.” The Los Angeles rapper was accepting song of the year for “Not Like Us,” which won five awards that night, including record of the year. Lamar would return the following year to pick up another five Grammys for his GNX album and its smash SZA collaboration “Luther,” which made him the first solo male artist to win record of the year in consecutive years. And GNX was nominated for album of the year in 2026 alongside Tyler, The Creator’s Chromakopia and Clipse’s Let God Sort Em Out — only the second time three rap albums were up for that prize in the same year. Of late, hip-hop has had a starring role on Music’s Biggest Night — but 2027 could be different. As it has for much of the streaming era, hip-hop reigned supreme in 2026 as the most consumed form of popular music, leading all genres in streams. Look a little closer, however, and its chart dominance has been slipping for years. title: Could This Rap Remix Trend Bring the Genre Back To the Charts?
summary: The Game, Meek Mill & Run the Jewels all remixed their own hits this summer. Did it move the needle?
body: When The Game recently decided he wanted to remix his 2005 hit “Hate It or Love It,” “Everybody thought that I was crazy,” he says. “They’re like, ‘This is a classic. You shouldn’t touch this. How are you going to make it better?’ And I thought to myself, ‘I love challenges, so how am I going to make it better?’” Without original collaborator 50 Cent on the hook — which two decades ago helped the song reach No. 2 on the Billboard Hot 100 — The Game brought Snoop Dogg into the fold, helping the Doggfather to write a verse that recalls his iconic counting flow on Dr. Dre’s 1992 G-funk classic “Nuthin’ but a ‘G’ Thang.” Both Game and Snoop made references to the original “Hate It or Love It,” while saluting West Coast legends including Nipsey Hussle, 2Pac and Ice Cube. A sample of Bobby Caldwell’s 1978 hit “What You Won’t Do for Love” — not present on the 2005 track — tied the new version together. title: This app gives Wear OS the Pixel music feature Apple already copied
summary: A new Wear OS app puts Pixel’s Now Playing where it always belonged.
body: TL;DR Now On Wrist brings your Pixel’s Now Playing results directly to a Wear OS smartwatch. It can show detected songs through notifications, a watch face complication, and a dedicated Wear OS tile. The app is available now on Google Play and works with Wear OS 3.0 or newer. Hearing a great song and having your Pixel identify it automatically is handy, but checking the result still usually means reaching for your phone. That feels a little clunky when you’re already wearing a smartwatch, which is where a new app called Now On Wrist comes in. It fixes that disconnect by bringing your Pixel’s Now Playing results directly to Wear OS. Now On Wrist doesn’t actually turn your smartwatch into a music-recognition device. Instead, it relies on the ambient music recognition happening on your phone, including Google’s Now Playing feature, and sends the identified song and artist to your wrist.

title: This iOS calendar app is side-stepping Android to embrace Googlebooks
summary: Will we be seeing more Googlebook exclusives further down the road?
body: TL;DR Fantastical launched as an iOS calendar app 15 years ago. It’s now finally coming to Google’s mobile devices with a Googlebook port. There’s a free version available, as well as several premium paid tiers. In a perfect world, the software we want to use would be available across all major platforms — but that’s just not the reality we live in. For multiple reasons, access is still a problem, and we’re always happy to see when a developer opens its doors to a new platform. Most of the time, that’s an iOS-only app finally becoming available for Android phones . Today, however, we might be looking at the first time ever an app skipped Android proper in order to launch a Googlebook edition. Fantastical is a powerful scheduling solution that got its start on Apple’s platforms, before eventually expanding to Windows. But in the 15 years it’s been around, the calendar app hasn’t been available for Google’s ecosystem. While it’s still not making the leap to Android phones and tablets — at least not yet — Fantastical is finally dipping a toe in the Google pool as developer Flexibits announces plans for a native Googlebook release.

title: I turned my phone into a thermal camera with the RISION Magic Pro
summary: Make any phone a surprisingly capable thermal camera with this simple USB-C accessory.
body: Credit: Robert Triggs / Android Authority As Android Authority’s resident testing engineer, I find temperatures a constant source of both success and failure for our gadget reviews. Whether a phone can sustain its fast charging speeds or deliver peak performance during prolonged gaming sessions depends on how well it dissipates heat. To see how modern gadgets fare, a dedicated temperature camera is often a very helpful solution, but it can be cumbersome, expensive, or come with poorer-quality optics. But what if I could make use of the countless phones I already have? Well, I’ve had the RISION Magic Pro () in the lab to see just how well that works. The RISION Magic Pro is a compact thermal camera, designed for professionals, that connects to your Android or iOS phone’s USB-C port. From there, you can control the camera via the RISON app, which provides a live temperature readout, screenshot capability, and a selection of customization options. The little USB-C module is eminently pocketable, but ships with a small carry case to keep it protected should you need to take it out and about.

title: Android Auto could soon stop working on millions of phones
summary: Android 10 users are starting to see warnings that support will end soon.
body: TL;DR Users on Android 10 are starting to receive warnings that Android Auto will soon stop working on their phones. The alerts suggest Google may be preparing to raise the minimum Android Auto requirement for wired connections to Android 11. Google hasn’t announced the change yet, and its support pages still list Android 9 Pie as the minimum for wired Android Auto. Android Auto has already left several older versions of Android behind over the years, and another cutoff now appears to be approaching. Google dropped support for Android 8 Oreo and older devices in 2022, then moved the minimum to Android 9 Pie in 2024 . Now, Android 10 users are starting to see warnings that their phones will soon stop working with Android Auto, suggesting Android 11 could become the next minimum requirement. Several users with older phones have recently reported seeing a notification when connecting to their cars that reads, “Phone will no longer be supported,” followed by a warning that Android Auto will soon stop working because the device cannot update to the required Android version.

title: Apple’s rumored smart display is a serious threat to Google Home — if it gets these things right
summary: Google should be terrified of Apple actually taking the smart home seriously.
body: Apple, Amazon, and Google are the big three companies in the smart home space. If we’re being honest, though, Amazon’s Echo and Google’s Nest ecosystems have dominated the smart home market for years — Apple’s HomeKit is only loosely relevant because of its first-party integration with iOS. Google’s smart home ecosystem in particular is the complete package, as the brand sells smart speakers, displays, cameras, thermostats, and more. By comparison, Apple relies on third-party accessory makers for almost everything in the HomeKit ecosystem. That’s about to change, at least in part. According to a report from Bloomberg , Apple is gearing up to launch two variants of a smart display this month. It’s part of a larger home refresh, kicked off with iOS 27, that is said to include a new Apple TV and a HomePod mini, too.

title: 5 Android phones you should buy instead of the iPhone 18 Pro Max
summary: Apple isn't the only tempting option.
body: It’s been a few weeks since Apple launched the iPhone 18 Pro Max , and this year, it’s more expensive than ever to get your hands on one. The ongoing RAM and memory crunch hasn’t helped, and while Apple certainly isn’t the only brand feeling the pinch, $1,299 for the base 256GB iPhone 18 Pro Max is still a lot of money. And that got me thinking about what else you could get for the same money. On the Android side, some seriously good phones don’t just compete with the iPhone 18 Pro Max — they offer features and experiences you really won’t get on Apple’s flagship. So, if I had $1,299 to spend on a phone today, these are the five Android phones I’d consider buying instead of the iPhone 18 Pro Max.

title: We’re witnessing a critical moment for Amazon Kindles
summary: Two steps forward, one step back.
body: Credit: Amazon To say that Amazon has had a rough year with the Kindle would be an understatement. Between sunsetting older e-reader models, making it harder to download purchased Kindle books, and introducing a series of changes that gave power users plenty to complain about, Amazon’s Kindle ecosystem was clearly going through a rough patch. It’s gotten to a point where plenty of users have started looking at Kobo or one of the many Android-powered e-readers instead. These alternatives offer many of the extras that Kindle fans have been asking for for years – physical buttons, support for more formats, and better customization. Basically, they offer more control over the device you paid for.

title: This Android flagship won our best iPhone 18 Pro alternative survey by a landslide

body: The iPhone 18 Pro and sundry broke cover last month, giving Apple smartphone fans their annual set of device upgrades. As good as the lineup looks this year, especially the Pro in its Burgundy colorway, it’ll be a tough buy for many, many people, especially readers of Android Authority . Naturally, our readership leans towards Android devices , but, given this bias, we wanted to know which phone you’d rather buy over the iPhone 18 Pro. My colleague Shimul Sood offered up her quintet of potentials , but which is our readers’ favorite? Well, there’s a landslide winner in our newest poll, and it’s not the Pixel 11 Pro .

title: I love the Pixel 11 Pro, but Google has 3 big problems to fix for the Pixel 12 Pro
summary: Google, this is what you need to do.
body: The Google Pixel 11 Pro is one of the best Android phones I’ve used this year. 11 years into the Pixel saga, Google has nailed just about everything with its flagship smartphones — from excellent hardware to top-tier cameras and unmatched software. However, as good as the Pixel 11 Pro may be, perfect it is not. In fact, it pretty clearly highlights three lingering issues that Google still hasn’t solved. title: Googlebooks have unlockable bootloader support, and there’s also good news for Magisk
summary: Support documents confirm easy bootloader unlocking, and Magisk developer has teased Magisk coming soon for the platform.
body: TL;DR Google has confirmed via an official support document that its new Googlebook laptops will feature unlockable bootloaders. The steps appear to be quite simple, almost Pixel-like. Magisk creator John Wu also announced that Magisk is coming to Googlebooks, with dedicated code and instructions releasing soon. This presumably opens the gate for easy root access. Unlocking the bootloader will allow for deep system modifications, performance tuning, ad blocking, and more, giving the Googlebook OS platform a competitive edge for power users. Google’s recently revealed Googlebook laptops may be steering the company’s vision toward a desktop future powered by Android, and, quite on brand, it seems the company still wants to honor its Android roots. A new support document confirms that Googlebooks will have unlockable bootloaders, and Magisk developer John Wu has also confirmed that Magisk is coming to Googlebooks, practically bringing easy root access to Google’s desktop-centric operating system. In a post on X , John Wu, the renowned developer behind Magisk and a Google employee, announced, “Magisk on Googlebook. New code and instructions will come in the following days.”

title: Google Maps has become nearly unusable for some Pixel 11 users on Android Auto
summary: Maps can flicker, freeze, or fall behind while the rest of Android Auto keeps working.
body: TL;DR Some Pixel 11 owners say Google Maps freezes, flickers, lags, or shows graphical glitches in Android Auto. The problem has been reported over both wired and wireless connections. Google support has escalated at least one report and is contacting affected users for more information, but there’s no confirmed fix yet. Android Auto has been serving up something close to a bug of the week lately. Google recently had to explain why Maps’ speedometer was disappearing , and it just fixed another long-running Android Auto signal bars issue . Now another navigation headache has been added to the pile, and this one appears to be hitting Google’s new Pixel 11 family. Several Pixel 11 owners across Reddit and the Android Auto community are reporting that Google Maps becomes choppy, freezes, flickers, or throws strange graphical artifacts on their car displays. For some, Maps repeatedly flickers and briefly turns into “pixelated black static,” while the YouTube Music panel and navigation overlays remain stable. This happens over both wired and wireless Android Auto.

body: “I want to be able to look at a rocket launch and say, ‘I touched a piece of this.’” That’s how Richard Spolzino describes the thing he’s chasing. Not a title, not a specific mission, not even NASA itself, just the ability to point at something real and know his work made it possible. At NASA’s Langley Research Center in Hampton, Virginia, Spolzino works within Moon Base’s mission architecture and systems interoperability effort, helping identify what NASA still doesn’t know about the Moon and Mars, and making sure that missing information gets found before it becomes a problem. Aerospace engineer Richard Spolzino Credit: NASA “ For me, it kept coming back to where can I have the most impact? Where can my work touch the most things? “ From History to Aerospace Spolzino didn’t set out to end up here. He started college as a history major. He switched to a physics track at Santa Clara University, thinking he’d end up in astrophysics. A research stint at Lick Observatory studying interstellar dust polarization taught him two things: the work was fascinating and, “I don’t think the staying-up-all-night thing…

title: I tried Duolingo for the first time in a year, and it’s worse than I thought
summary: This isn't the Duolingo I remember.
body: I used to be a dedicated Duolingo user. I logged in every day, hit my daily quota, and became a little more proficient at a new language. About a year ago, though, I gave up on the language-learning app. Duolingo became a shell of its former self; its lessons became redundant and the daily tasks repetitive. I didn’t feel like I was learning anything new, which defeats the purpose of a language tutor. I eventually uninstalled it. Sadly, this meant losing my 500+ daily streak .

title: After a month with the Galaxy Z Fold 8, every other Android phone feels wrong
summary: A month with the Galaxy Z Fold 8 has quietly ruined every other phone for me.
body: Credit: Tushar Mehta / Android Authority I’ve had the Galaxy Z Fold 8 for nearly a month now, and I’ve purposely avoided using any other phone during that time. I had high hopes — and expectations — for the phone even before its launch, primarily because I have long wanted to use small phones that don’t feel sub-premium. What I didn’t expect was how hard it would hit me to switch back to a “regular” phone. Every moment I have spent with the Fold 8 has changed my perception of what a phone should feel like in the hand. Rather than thinking of the Fold 8 in terms such as “short,” “stout,” or “wide,” I have come to feel that every other phone is too tall and unwieldy. For that reason, I don’t see myself (willingly) giving up the Fold 8 — or returning to phones with displays bigger than 6.7 inches, which, unfortunately, has become the norm for a flagship Android experience.

title: YouTube is cleaning up one of the worst parts of Shorts
summary: Giving low-effort Shorts less room to breathe.
body: TL;DR YouTube is updating Shorts recommendations to prioritize original content and reduce the reach of low-effort reuploads from other creators. Reused clips can still surface if creators add meaningful commentary, editing, storytelling, or another original angle. For viewers, the change should make the Shorts feed feel less repetitive, while creators clipping their own long-form videos likely won’t be affected. YouTube Shorts have never exactly been a fan-favorite feature. From users wanting Shorts to be a standalone app, to YouTube itself letting users set their daily Shorts feed limit to zer o, there’s no shortage of signs pointing to how unhappy many users are with how aggressively short-form video has been pushed across the platform. One of the big reasons behind the disdain is the sheer amount of slop that floods the Shorts feed . YouTube knows that, and it is now starting to prioritize original content on Shorts. Announced by the streaming giant in a blog post this week, YouTube is updating its recommendation system specific to Shorts to reduce the reach of re-uploaded content, where videos taken from other creators are reposted without adding anything meaningful.

body: TL;DR Google is testing biometric authentication before password autofill in Chrome for Android. The feature has returned in Chrome Canary after Google previously tested and pulled a similar implementation before stable release. The flag works for some users, but it didn’t trigger on a Pixel 8 in testing, suggesting the rollout is still limited or incomplete. Google Chrome on Android does a lot of heavy lifting when it comes to passwords. With Google Password Manager, the browser lets you seamlessly add and save new passwords, complete with the option to use strong suggested options. And when you return to a website where you’ve previously saved your login credentials, Chrome can automatically fill them in for you. As convenient as that is, Google wants to add an additional step to that process. Google is testing a new feature where Chrome on Android will require biometric authentication before it autofills passwords.

title: PS3 games hogging storage on your Android device? This ARMSX3 feature is for you.
summary: ARMSX3 now plays CHD files, which delivers much smaller file sizes than conventional ISO files.
body: Credit: Hadlee Simons / Android Authority TL;DR A recent ARMSX3 update has introduced support for playing games in the CHD format. This compressed format can shave gigabytes off your PS3 game files. The update also offers improved frame generation and fewer stutters in certain PS3 games. PlayStation 3 emulation on Android made major strides in recent months thanks to the ARMSX3 app. However, one potential issue is that PS3 games can hog a ton of space on your Android device. Fortunately, a recent ARMSX3 update helps address this issue. The team behind ARMSX3 recently released v1.0.6 of the emulator on GitHub , and it now supports CHD disc images. CHD (Compressed Hunks of Data) is a compression format that delivers smaller file sizes than conventional ISOs.

title: Google Meet and Microsoft Teams just got better at working together
summary: Your meeting room no longer has to pick a side.
body: TL;DR Google Meet and Microsoft Teams can now work across supported Android-based meeting-room hardware. Meet hardware can join Teams calls, while Android-based Microsoft Teams Rooms can join Google Meet meetings. The feature began rolling out on October 1 and should reach eligible Google Workspace customers within 1-3 days. If you’ve ever walked into a meeting room only to realize the call is on Microsoft Teams while the room is set up for Google Meet , you’ll know how unnecessarily complicated something as simple as joining a video call can become. Google started addressing that problem last month when it previewed a new interoperability feature that would let Meet and Teams hardware work together. The idea was to remove some of the usual barriers between the two platforms. With the feature, a meeting room equipped with Android-based Google Meet hardware could join a Microsoft Teams call, while a Microsoft Teams Room running Android could do the same with a Google Meet call. So, if your company primarily uses Meet but a client sends you a Teams invite, you wouldn’t have to reach for a laptop or switch rooms just because everyone happens to be using a different video conferencing…

title: A strange YouTube login bug is locking some users out of the website
summary: Reports suggest an account-specific sign-in bug could be affecting multiple browsers.
body: TL;DR Some YouTube users can’t sign in on web browsers, even though their Google accounts work normally elsewhere. Reports span multiple browsers and computers, with affected accounts still working in the YouTube mobile and TV apps. The issue has been escalated for investigation, but Google hasn’t publicly explained what’s causing it or when a fix may arrive. YouTube only recently put out one login fire after fixing a bug that locked some viewers out on TVs and gaming consoles . But while that problem was getting attention, another sign-in headache appears to have been quietly frustrating a much smaller group of YouTube users on the web. Reports stretching back roughly two weeks describe accounts that work normally across other Google services but refuse to sign in to YouTube in a browser. A Reddit user said clearing cookies, switching browsers, using Incognito mode, changing passwords, and even trying another computer made no difference. Their affected accounts still worked in YouTube’s mobile app.
